3. The appellant filed Title Suit No.55 of 1993 against the respondents for declaration of title and for further declaration that the registered dead No.6007 executed by the defendant No. 1 in favour of the defendant No.2 on 17.02.1992 and registered on 23.06.1992 was forged, collusive, fraudulent and the same was not binding upon the plaintiff stating that the suit land originally belonged to the landlords of Kashimpur namely, Sarada Prossad Roy Chowdhury and others and C. S. record-of-right was duly prepared In their names. The suit land was vested in the Government and the plaintiff has been possessing the same The defendants, creating some rent receipts aria pattannama to grab the suit land of the government, claimed that they are the owners of the suit land. The defendants, in collusion with some employees of collectorate office, managed to change S.A. khatian by tempering and removing pages of volume books. During R.S. operation, the defendants, in collusion with settlement employees, managed to get their names recorded in R.S. Khatian collusively End fraudulently. On 17.11.1992, the appellant came to know further that the defendant No. I, as an executant, created the impugned kabala dated 17.02.1992 in respect of the suit land in favour of the defendant No.2 fraudulently. The plaintiff, thereafter, inquired into the matter and found that the defendants fraudulently managed to record the suit land in their names in both S.A. and R.S. Khatians and also created the impugned kabala deed in respect of the suit land though the suit land was the khas land of the government. Hence, was the suit. 

 5. The trial Court, on consideration of the evidence adduced by both the parties, decreed the suit making observations that the contesting defendants failed to prove the alleged settlement of the suit land in favour of their predecessors and that the S.A. and R.S. khatians were erroneous and created by manipulating the government documents. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the contesting defendant nos.22-23 preferred Title Appeal No.121 of 2001 and the contesting defendant Nos. 1 and 2 preferred Title Appeal No.135 of 2001 and the appellate Court by the judgment and decree dated 15.07.2004, allowed the appeals upon reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court and dismissed the suit holding that the plaintiff could not prove its right, title and possession in the suit land by adducing any evidence. Against the judgment and being Nos. 3948 of 2004, 28 of 2010 and 29 if 2010 were filed in the High Court Division. The High Court Division discharged all the Rules. Against the said judgment and order, the Government preferred this appeal and leave petitions. 

 7. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Nurul Amin, Senior Advocate appearing for respondent Nos.16, 19 & 20-21 in Civil Appeal No.183 of 2015 submits that during the S.A. operation the land measuring an area of 16.46 acres under C.S. Plot No.271 was divided in 3 (three) S.A. Khatians being Nos. 1, 51 and 114. The land measuring 1.04 acres of S.A. khatian No.1 was recorded in the name of the government, 7.42 acres 3f S.A Khatian no. 51 was recorded in the name of Mozirunnessa and 8 acres in S.A Khatian No. 114 recorded in the name of Nazimuddin, predecessor-ininterest of some of the defendants. Those Khatians were exhibited marked as Exhibit-Chha-1, 2 and 3. R.S Khatians were also pre-pared accordingly (Exhibit Chha-4-6).
